item.title: 【Software Testing Weekly - Issue 313 - May 18th 2026】软件测试周刊 - 第 313 期 - 2026 年 5 月 18 日
item.description:
【

COMMENT

Welcome to the 313th issue!

Looking to expand your QA knowledge?

I recently stumbled upon QA Decoded.

It's a fantastic collection of 25+ learning modules ranging from basics to advanced topics.

Kudos to Md. Farhan Labib for putting it together.

Happy testing! 🙂

Dawid Dylowicz

Sponsored Link

Automate Test Execution... Without Test Automation

Lynqa executes your test with AI and generates step-by-step reports. No code, no rewriting, no maintenance, no recording. Try it now with 10 free executions.

smartesting.com

NEWS

AI Is Doing the Testing Now

It's hard to disagree with Brijesh Deb who points out that although it's easier to broaden the test coverage now, it can't replace human judgment and mitigate risks quite as well.

Moreover, Betty Lin continues the great series of articles on QA Meets AI (Part 5): Correctness and Judgment Are Not the Same Thing.

medium.com

QA's Bottleneck Just Moved. Most Teams Haven't Noticed.

A thoughtful observation from James Kip on how we should approach testing, proposing a split where we own the behavioural acceptance criteria while AI owns the technical implementation.

Similarly, Elizabeth Rubino shares how QA Is Evolving — And Tests Aren't the Point.

medium.com

So you want to be an SDET

Kevin Roe makes a good point. Don't become a software engineer who happens to test — become a tester who happens to code. Kevin also wrote a good follow-up defining The Ideal Team SDET.

Moreover, Marina Jordão warns about Why QAs Who Only Automate Stop Growing.

goforthandtest.com

The Test Manager's Guide: From Chaos to Predictable Quality

Abdul Osman started an insightful series of articles advising test managers and leaders on how to approach testing and quality. You can already read the following parts two, three and four.

Similarly, Joshua Bihun shares some thoughts on What to Document First When You’re Building or Inheriting a QA Practice.

medium.com

What Good Governance Actually Looks Like

Simon Prior has been on a streak of writing great articles recently and this one is no exception. This time, it's about solid principles for practical AI governance.

In relation to that, Andrii Lysenko rightly points out The QA work AI can't do.

leadtestinclude.com

What Makes Good Context For AI-Generated Tests?

If you want AI to do a more accurate job for test generation, follow Puja Jagani's advice on how to properly provide it with the relevant information.

At the same time, Sachin Koirala describes The Intent Gap: How We Learned to Ship Fast and Forget Everything.

medium.com

AUTOMATION

I Built a Multi-Agent QA Documentation System with Claude Code — Here's What I Actually Learned

If you want to learn how to create an Ai solution that turns Jira tickets into a full test plan, check out Heramb Bhor's reflection on what worked and what didn't.

In relation to that, Brad DerManouelian shares interesting thoughts on Why Your Test Scripts Don't Belong in Your Test Case Management Tool.

medium.com

The Philosophy of Automated Tests: Management, Maintenance and Flakiness

Ever wondered how others handle flaky tests? Vladimir Smirnov describes how their team at Exante does it at scale by sorting failures by priority and keeping a regression test suite healthy.

Moreover, Kevin Roe shares a story on why Most Test Frameworks Are Over-Engineered

medium.com

Where Goal-Based Agentic Testing Sits in the Mobile Automation Pyramid

Thinking of adding AI agents to your mobile test setup? Russell Morley put together a good guide on how to make it work with existing test layers.

russmorley.net

Your Load Test Passed. Your Server Crashed. Here's Why (Little's Law Fix Inside)

It's easy to add load tests, but it's not easy to design them right. Jenish Patel gives tons of practical tips on numbers that matter and what to consider in users' behaviour.

medium.com

Sponsored Link

QA Takes the Lead is Back on May 27th

Now more than ever, it's time to transform the way we talk about QA, and align with what business and leadership really cares about. Join us for QA Takes the Lead — a 2nd edition of this free online conference to learn from industry thought leaders about the new role of QA. Register for free!

practitest.com

TOOLS

A Comprehensive Guide to Benchmarking LLMs with AWS Labs’ LLMeter

How would you test LLM-based apps for performance? NaveenKumar Namachivayam wrote a handy guide to AWS's LLMeter, showing how to set up experiments, run multi-client load tests and build a live dashboard for cost-tracking.

Talking about testing LLMs, Fidaa Berrjeb shares an interesting story of how they approached Testing a GenAI voice assistant.

qainsights.com

Claude Code Hooks as a Test Quality Gate

Sometimes your test may contain hardcoded waits and missing assertions. Irfan Mujagić demonstrates simple shell hooks for Claude Code that flag these issues as soon as they save the test file.

Moreover, Mukta Agarwal shares examples from personal experience on How I Use Claude Skills for QA tasks.

thegreenreport.blog

How I Debug Appium Test Failures Without Inspector

Testing mobile apps with Appium? Josphine Job shares a few tips on debugging issues, followed by an explanation of Why Appium Scroll Fails Across Device Sizes.

medium.com

Playwright Sharding and Docker: How I Cut My Test Suite from 47 Minutes to 8 Minutes

If you want to cut the execution time of your Playwright tests, Pramod Dutta wrote a step-by-step guide on splitting a 312-test Playwright suite into shards running in Docker.

This is followed by another insightful article describing Why Most Self-Healing Implementations Fail in Production.

scrolltest.com

The Cypress i18n Mistake: Testing Words Instead of Meaning — i18next is your partner

If you're testing apps that support many languages, Sebastian Clavijo Suero advises using stable selectors alongside i18next keys to reliably verify translated messages.

dev.to

VIDEOS

How I use Notebook LM for Software Testing and more

In this 17-minute video, Daniel Knott demonstrates handy use cases for Google's NotebookLM in QA-related work that's especially good at processing a lot of information.

youtube.com

Question Hospital: Testing and AI #1

With AI now fully embedded in software development work, many of us wonder about its use cases and impact in testing. That's why James Bach, Jon Bach and Michael Bolton came together to answer the testing community's questions and recorded an insightful, one-hour discussion.

youtube.com

AND...

Good old times... 😅

Thanks for reading!

If you enjoy this newsletter and find it helpful in becoming a better tester, please consider sharing it with others.

Dawid Dylowicz

goforthandtest.com

leadtestinclude.com

同时，Sachin Koirala 描述了意图差距：我们如何学会快速交付并忘记一切。

medium.com

自动化

我用 Claude 代码构建了一个多代理 QA 文档系统 - 这是我实际学到的内容

medium.com

自动化测试的哲学：管理、维护和不稳定

有没有想过其他人如何处理不稳定的测试？ Vladimir Smirnov 描述了 Exante 的团队如何通过按优先级对故障进行排序并保持回归测试套件健康。

此外，Kevin Roe 分享了一个关于为什么大多数测试框架都过度设计

的故事

基于目标的代理测试在移动自动化金字塔中的位置

您的负载测试已通过。您的服务器崩溃了。这就是为什么（利特尔定律修复内部）

添加负载测试很容易，但正确设计它们并不容易。 Jenish Patel 提供了大量关于重要数字以及在用户行为中应考虑的因素的实用技巧。

medium.com

赞助商链接

QA 主导工作将于 5 月 27 日回归

现在比以往任何时候都更需要改变我们谈论质量检查的方式，并与业务和领导层真正关心的事情保持一致。加入我们的QA 引领——这是免费在线会议的第二版，向行业思想领袖了解 QA 的新角色。 免费注册！

practitest.com

工具

使用 AWS 实验室的 LLMeter 对 LLM 进行基准测试的综合指南

您将如何测试基于 LLM 的应用程序的性能？ NaveenKumar Namachivayam 编写了 AWS LLMeter 的便捷指南，展示了如何设置实验、运行多客户端负载测试以及构建用于成本跟踪的实时仪表板。

qainsights.com

Claude 代码挂钩作为测试质量门

有时您的测试可能包含硬编码的等待和丢失的断言。 Irfan Mujagić 演示了 Claude Code 的简单 shell 挂钩，这些挂钩在保存测试文件后立即标记这些问题。

使用 Appium 测试移动应用程序？ Josphine Job 分享了一些有关调试问题的技巧，并解释了为什么 Appium Scroll 在不同设备尺寸上都会失败。

item.title: 【Software Testing Weekly - Issue 312 - May 9th 2026】软件测试周刊 - 第 312 期 - 2026 年 5 月 9 日
item.description:
【

COMMENT

Welcome to the 312th issue!

While I was browsing Reddit, this discussion caught my eye:

What's one QA career move you made that gave the biggest ROI?

There are a lot of different points of view, examples and lessons on investing in specific skills, changing companies and going into management.

Hope you'll find some inspiration there, as well as in the rest of the news I'm sharing with you today.

Happy testing! 🙂

Dawid Dylowicz

Sponsored Link

AI in QA: what's working, what's not, what's next

With one day to go for Breakpoint 2026, most QA teams have moved past the question of whether to use AI and are sitting with the harder one of how to use it well. Avinash Ahuja from NVIDIA, Keith Klain, and Ashley Hunsberger are on stage talking about scaling AI, where agentic workflows actually deliver, and what it takes to move past the pilot. The conference runs free and virtual from May 12 to 14. Save your spot!

browserstack.com

NEWS

Adventures in 30 Years in Engineering Productivity

Carlos Arguelles looks back on three decades of working on developer tools, testing infra, canary monitoring and bug dedup at Microsoft, Amazon and Google. A great read packed with stories, lessons learned and practical advice.

On top of that, Stuart Thomas describes The forgotten part of quality: paying attention to production.

medium.com

How Junior Engineers Can Build Real Skills While Using AI

AI is a huge enabler for all engineers, including juniors. Dennis Martinez explains how they can leverage it, sharing simple advice like slowing down and writing code by hand. Applicable to testers, too.

The good news is that "Silly Questions" Are Almost Never Silly in the age of AI, as [Imen Naguez](https://www.linkedin.com/in/imen-naguez-qa/ correctly points out.

dev-tester.com

Shift Left Did Not Fix It

It's a thought-provoking article by Brijesh Deb about the actual benefits of shifting testing left and why getting testers involved earlier doesn't always lead to reduced risk later in the process.

Moreover, Lisa Crispin and Janet Gregory share some good thoughts on DORA and AI Capabilities.

medium.com

Testing from first principles: when there is no guide to follow

Peter Wilson shares lessons from testing ML, mobile and CI/CD pipelines, advising on how to rely on fundamentals when testing.

Also, Alan Page tells us to beware of making The Five Reasonable Mistakes — How leaders build low-quality systems without trying.

medium.com

The Human in the Loop Isn't Going Anywhere: They're Just Moving Up

While AI can write the test code, humans should still decide what to test and why. Simon Prior explains why business context, risk judgment and independent validation are best done by people.

At the same time, Faris Kurnia shares a reflection about Rethinking QA: Are We Still Testing, or Just Tracking?

leadtestinclude.com

AUTOMATION

Anyone Can Build. Almost No One Can Maintain: The Real Cost of AI Coding

While it's trivial to create code nowadays, Maksim Laptev points out that the challenges of maintaining it are still there, based on a story of vibe coding a trading bot.

Also, someone asked on Reddit: Are you actually using AI in test automation?

medium.com

Claude Code For QA — The Agentic Workflow That Will Save You 100+ Hours

Art Krylov demonstrates a Claude Code setup with sub-agents for creating test cases, manual runs and API automation, using MCP for Jira, Postman and more.

Furthermore, Swati Seela shares valuable Lessons Learned from Building an AI-Enabled Test Automation Repo.

medium.com

Common Mistakes in Performance Testing (And How to Fix Them)

Doing load tests? Oleh Koren lists seven mistakes that can impact your results, with checklists and fixes you can apply on your next run.

Moreover, Tito Irfan Wibisono describes Chaos Engineering: How Software QA Engineers Test Resilience in Distributed Microservices.

medium.com

Testing LLM Based Products: A Practical Guide for Delivery and Quality Teams

If you test LLM-powered systems, Alejandro Sierra gives advice on using a four-layer evaluation stack with code examples in PromptFoo, DeepEval, Ragas, LangSmith and Braintrust.

Similarly, Max Vornovskykh shares an insightful piece about Building a Robust Evaluation System for 32 AI Agents Across 4 Platforms.

medium.com

TOOLS

Confessions of a Recovering Selenium Developer

Wondering why Kevin Roe moved from Selenium to Playwright? He walks through the things that piled up over the years, leading to the decision.

On the other hand, Puja Jagani describes how to use WebDriver BiDi for Test Automation: Preload Scripts and Test Efficiency.

goforthandtest.com

Creating a Playwright framework with AI

Callum Akehurst-Ryan describes building a Playwright end-to-end framework with Claude Code and getting broad coverage of high-priority workflows and why keeping human-in-the-loop was key in making it work.

Also, Ekki Syam Sugiardi demonstrates an example of How I Built an AI Agent That Writes Playwright Tests From a GitHub Issue.

cakehurstryan.com

Modeling UI Flows as JSON: A Data-Driven Approach to Cypress Test Architecture

Want to make your Cypress tests easy to maintain? John Ringler shares a three-layer setup where each UI flow lives as JSON and a single dispatcher runs every step type.

On top of that, Gleb Bahmutov compares Cypress cy.prompt Vs Recording Vs Coding.

medium.com

@playwright-labs/reporter-slack: Rich Slack Notifications for Playwright Test Runs

If you want to get your Playwright test results in Slack, Vitali Haradkou shares how to achieve that with a @playwright-labs/playwright-slack extension.

blog-vitaliharadkous-projects.vercel.app

Your First Appium Test: A Complete End-to-End Guide for Android and iOS

Mayvin Ramasawmy shows what it takes to run the same Appium tests across Android and iOS. Login, swipes, scrolls, drag-and-drop, plus a side-by-side look at every spot the two platforms split.

You can also learn more about using the Appium Inspector and Appium Execute Methods.

mobile-automation.io

AND...

Testing, actually... 😂

Thanks for reading!

If you enjoy this newsletter and find it helpful in becoming a better tester, please consider sharing it with others.

Dawid Dylowicz

评论

欢迎来到第312期！

当我浏览 Reddit 时，这个讨论引起了我的注意：

您做出的 QA 职业举措中哪一项带来了最大的投资回报率？

关于投资特定技能、更换公司和进入管理层，有很多不同的观点、例子和教训。

希望您能从中找到一些灵感，以及我今天与您分享的其他新闻。

测试愉快！ 🙂

大卫·迪洛维奇

赞助商链接

质量检查中的人工智能：什么有效，什么无效，下一步是什么

距离 2026 年断点 比赛还有一天，大多数 QA 团队已经超越了是否使用 AI 的问题，转而思考如何更好地使用它这一更难的问题。来自 NVIDIA 的 Avinash Ahuja、Keith Klain 和 Ashley Hunsberger 在台上谈论扩展 AI、代理工作流程实际提供的功能以及如何超越试点。该会议于 5 月 12 日至 14 日免费虚拟举行。保留席位！

browserstack.com

新闻

工程生产力 30 年来的历险

Carlos Arguelles 回顾了 Microsoft、Amazon 和 Google 三十年来在开发人员工具、测试基础设施、金丝雀监控和错误删除方面的工作。这是一本精彩的读物，充满了故事、经验教训和实用建议。

除此之外，Stuart Thomas 描述了质量中被遗忘的部分：关注生产。

medium.com

初级工程师如何在使用人工智能的同时培养真正的技能

人工智能对于所有工程师（包括初级工程师）来说都是一个巨大的推动者。 Dennis Martinez 解释了他们如何利用它，分享简单的建议，例如放慢速度和手动编写代码。也适用于测试人员。

好消息是，正如 [Imen Naguez](https://www.linkedin.com/in/imen-naguez-qa/ 正确指出的那样，在人工智能时代，“愚蠢的问题”几乎从来都不是愚蠢的。

dev-tester.com

左移未修复

这是一篇由 Brijesh Deb 撰写的关于实际好处的发人深省的文章测试左移的原因以及为什么让测试人员尽早参与并不总能降低流程后期的风险。

此外，Lisa Crispin 和 Janet Gregory 分享了一些关于 DORA 和 AI 功能的好想法。

medium.com

从第一原则开始测试：没有可遵循的指南

Peter Wilson 分享了测试 ML、移动和 CI/CD 管道的经验教训，并就测试时如何依赖基本原理提供了建议。

此外，Alan Page 告诉我们要谨防犯五个合理的错误 - 领导者如何在不尝试的情况下构建低质量的系统。

medium.com

循环中的人不会去任何地方：他们只是向上移动

虽然人工智能可以编写测试代码，但人类仍然应该决定测试什么以及为什么。 Simon Prior 解释了为什么业务背景、风险判断和独立验证最好由人来完成。

同时，Faris Kurnia 分享了关于重新思考 QA：我们还在测试还是只是跟踪？

leadtestinclude.com

自动化

任何人都可以构建。几乎无人能维护：人工智能编码的真实成本

虽然现在创建代码很简单，但 Maksim Laptev 指出，根据 Vivi 编码交易机器人的故事，维护代码的挑战仍然存在。

此外，有人在 Reddit 上问：你真的在测试自动化中使用人工智能吗？

medium.com

克劳德 QA 代码 - 代理工作流程将为您节省 100 多个小时

Art Krylov 演示了带有子代理的 Claude Code 设置，用于使用 MCP for Jira、Postman 等创建测试用例、手动运行和 API 自动化。

此外，Swati Seela 分享了宝贵的从构建支持 AI 的测试自动化存储库中学到的经验教训。

medium.com

性能测试中的常见错误（以及如何修复它们）

COMMENT

Welcome to the 311th issue!

"May the 4th be with you!"

Or so goes the popular saying for today.

And we've been given more force than we ever had — thanks to AI.

But with great power comes great responsibility.

And that's what I want to remind you with these three fantastic articles from tech leaders:

  • Vibe Coding Works Until It Doesn't. AI-Generated PRs Carry 1.7× More Issues by Alex Svystun (CTO)
  • Here Come the Bugs by Don Neufeld (CEO)
  • The AI Quality Paradox by David Stockton (VP Eng)

Happy testing!

Dawid Dylowicz

Sponsored Link

How QA Leaders Are Actually Using AI To Improve Software Quality

Most teams aren't struggling with whether to use AI, they're struggling with how to use it well. At Breakpoint, speakers from NVIDIA, Microsoft, KPMG, and more cover the real decisions quality engineering leaders are facing: how to scale AI across your org, where agentic and autonomous QA workflows actually deliver, and what it takes to move past the pilot. If you're figuring out where AI fits in your QA workflow, this is a practical starting point. May 12–14. Save your spot!

browserstack.com

NEWS

How to Triage Bugs Without Losing Your Mind (or Your Team's Trust)

Joshua Bihun introduces a score-based bug triage approach that takes both severity and priority into account.

In relation to that, Okeke Kenneth gives several handy tips on How to write a Bug Report that Developers actually act on.

medium.com

QA Meets AI (Part 1): Why I Started This Experiment

What does it feel like to test alongside AI through a full QA cycle? Betty Lin kicks off a hands-on series with honest remarks on where AI helps and where instinct takes over. You can already read part 2, part 3 and part 4.

Similarly, Jason Arbon started a series: Day 1 • Evaluating How Well AI Can Find Bugs.

medium.com

Quality Engineering Is Not Testing

And testing is not quality. Michael Bolton points out a problem with calling testers quality engineers and pushes back on the rebranding trend.

Moreover, Callum Akehurst-Ryan suggests that You're not ready for Quality Engineering while Luke Lattimer-Rogers says that You don't want Quality Engineers.

developsense.com

Will AI Replace Software Testers? The Hidden Expertise That AI Cannot Replicate

Don't worry — Ujjwal Kumar Singh shares that the strengths of testers are unlikely to be replaced by AI.

However, you may want to learn from Julia Kocbek about How to approach AI and stay sane.

tricentis.com

You're Testing AI Wrong

There are some good points brought up by Simon Prior on how to test and not to test LLM-powered applications, followed by advice: Don't Just Test the Output… Challenge the Reasoning.

There's also a great reminder from James Bach that Responsibility is the Human Moat.

leadtestinclude.com

AUTOMATION

Test Scaffold Writing Took Me Two Hours Per Feature. Three AI Agents Cut That to Eleven Minutes

Rohit Kshirsagar describes building an AI-powered solution of three agents for ticket reading, component analysis and scaffold test implementation.

Furthermore, Andrii Lysenko advises how to handle cases when Documentation exists. The agent doesn't read it.

medium.com

The Flaky Tests Truce

If a test passes on retry, don't delete it. It might be telling you about a flaky bug, not a flaky test. Kevin Roe makes a strong case for retries with receipts.

Similarly, Gil Zilberfeld describes The Flaky Test Files: The Case of the State Pollution.

goforthandtest.com

Thin Specs, Fat Models: A Page Object Pattern That Survives Real-World UI Changes

A handy pattern from Higor Mesquita for anyone using Playwright or Cypress, advising to move locators, waits and flow details into the model so specs are easier to understand.

Also, Swati Seela demonstrates that You Don't Need AI to Repair Your Broken Locators. You Can Do It Too.

medium.com

Why F.I.R.S.T. Testing Still Wins After 20 Years

Fernanda Nadhiftya revisits the Fast, Isolated, Repeatable, Self-validating and Timely test principles and demonstrates them with examples.

Moreover, Mochamad Syahrial Alzaidan briefly describes The AAA Pattern: A Simple Way to Write Better Tests.

medium.com

Why Your CI Test Suite Keeps Getting Slower

Is your CI test suite getting slower? Dennis Martinez explains why this happens, which metrics to track and how to fix the worst offenders before execution time increases.

dev-tester.com

TOOLS

API Spector a new Open Source API Testing Tool

Alan Richardson shares a first look at API Spector — an open source tool for HTTP and WebSocket testing, with imports from Postman, Insomnia, Bruno and OpenAPI, plus mock servers and contract testing.

Moreover, John Ringler showcases how to perform Automated API Testing with Jest, Supertest, and Docker.

eviltester.com

Intercept Everything: API Logging Middleware for Playwright

If your Playwright tests fail in CI with no request or response data to debug, Viatsheslav Pashanin suggests adding a logging middleware that attaches every API call to the HTML report.

Also, Vitaliy Potapov wrote another insightful article about Playwright in Pictures: Why Workers Restart?.

medium.com

MCP Servers for Test Automation: 4 Practical Use Cases (Jira, GitHub, Playwright)

Want to try MCP servers in your testing workflow? Michał Ślęzak shows four practical use cases of popular tools and points out the security and token costs you should watch for.

Additionally, Andrew Knight shares BDD Gherkin Guidelines for AI Coding and Testing which you can find directly here.

testingplus.me

Stop Manual Testing! How Claude Code + Maestro MCP Disrupt App Dev

Testing mobile apps? Ewan Mak shares a hands-on look at Maestro MCP, including an honest opinion on the 70-80% first-pass accuracy and iOS WebView gaps.

Furthermore, Prasenjit Sinha gives advice on building A Layered Mobile Testing Strategy for Long-Term Stability.

medium.com

Vibe Testing with Playwright MCP: Testing UX with AI Agents

Mohammad Faisal Khatri shows how to use Playwright MCP to test the feel of an app, not just the functions. Good walkthrough with prompts, generated code and a refactoring checklist.

Similarly, Rakesh Karkare describes in detail How I Built a Local AI Browser Agent Using Python + Ollama (LLM Model) + Playwright MCP.

medium.com

VIDEOS

April 2026 USA QA (Quality Assurance) Jobs Update

Alex Khvastovich continues an insightful series analysing the QA job market and shares data-driven insights from the last month in 12 minutes.

youtube.com

Talking about Test Stuff

There are some great insights into testing and quality from Alan Page who recently did three podcasts across various channels.

substack.com

AND...

This is AGI... 😂

Thanks for reading!

If you enjoy this newsletter and find it helpful in becoming a better tester, please consider sharing it with others.

Dawid Dylowicz

COMMENT

Welcome to the 310th issue!

The most recent ThoughtWork's Technology Radar is out and it's worth checking out.

It's a biannual snapshot of recommendations for tools, techniques, platforms, languages and frameworks from one of the most respected consulting companies.

It's great not only for spotting trends but also for identifying potential risks and dangers.

And if you're wondering what it means, Patrick Prill wrote a great summary — The Tech Radar is Blinking Red.

Happy testing!

Dawid Dylowicz

Sponsored Link

The Selenium creator on AI testing, BiDi, and what's real

If you've written a Selenium test, you've used something Jason Huggins built. At Breakpoint 2026, he's talking about where testing goes from here: BiDi, the shift-left rethink, and the gap between AI demos and what your sprint actually looks like. Join online for free on May 12–14. Save your spot!

browserstack.com

NEWS

A 6 Year Reflection on Software Quality, Doubt, and the Career You Actually Build

How does a quality engineer's job actually change with experience? Shubham Sharma looks back and reflects on the perception of quality, imposter syndrome and why senior engineers tolerate uncertainty better.

Moreover, Swati Seela shares her point of view on What Makes a Good QA Lead.

medium.com

A Practical Mental Model for Modern Testing

The author, whom I unfortunately couldn't identify, shared a really good, in-depth article with practical advice on how to think about each layer of tests the right way.

Similarly, Keith Klain brings up a few good points on Thinking, Fast and No.

medium.com

Cognitive Automation: This Isn't About How Fast You Can Generate Scripts

Are your AI-generated tests actually catching bugs? Simon Prior prompts quality leaders to use AI as a thinking partner for risk and strategy rather than a faster way to write flaky tests.

Simon also wrote a good article about Quality Culture: Shared Ownership Is Harder Now, Not Easier.

leadtestinclude.com

I've figured out where I fit in the AI era

A great, thoughtful read from Vernon Richards on how the tester role is evolving from hands-on work to coaching the team and guiding AI agents.

At the same time, Gary Hawkes explains Why Quality Engineers Matter in the AI Era.

substack.com

The Waterfall Strikes Back

Patrick Prill observed a funny pattern — Spec-Driven Development asks devs to write perfect specs upfront, which is the same thing we admitted we were bad at during the Waterfall era, before Agile came.

So where does it lead? Simon followed up with another article: Are We Building the Right Thing, or How GenAI Made Us Forget to Ask.

wordpress.com

AUTOMATION

AI and Testing: Evaluating Conversations

If you're testing AI-powered solutions, Jeff Nyman has a practical guide on using DeepEvals to check if a model holds its thread across a full multi-turn conversation.

testerstories.com

APIs Are Predictable. AI Isn't. Here’s What I Built

Want to stop AI from writing shallow API tests that just check for a 200 response? Wendy Erdheim-Poch shares a step-by-step workflow that scans routes, asks the right questions and reviews its own output.

Furthermore, Josphine Job shares good advice on Why Every QA Should Build Their Own AI Workspace.

medium.com

How to Handle Failing Tests Caused by a Known Bug

While it's easy to comment out a broken test, it's never a good idea. David Mello demonstrates how to use a skip pattern instead with bug ticket links and ready-to-use snippets for Jest, Playwright, pytest and JUnit.

Moreover, Swati Seela wrote a thoughtful article about Retries in Test Automation: Safety Net or Silent Problem?

davidmello.com

My 2 Cents: I'll gladly spend them to stop staring at test logs

Tired of trying to figure out if a failing test is flaky or showing an actual problem? Giuseppe Donati shares how trivago built an AI helper that does that work for them.

trivago.com

Optimizing the wrong part of the testing process

Chris Kenst inherited a 2,500-test Cypress suite that takes 45 hours to run and explains why automating everything leads to pain.

Similarly, Jitesh Gosai explains well When quantity leads to quality.

kenst.com

Treating the UI as a Contract: Eliminating the Wait in Modern Development

Want testing to start on day one instead of waiting until the end? David Ingraham and Leonardo Lanni wrote a thoughtful article explaining how a UI skeleton with mocked data lets front-end, back-end, and QA move at the same time.

On that note, Marko Churlinoski explains why we should Stop Writing New Tests. Supercharge the Ones You Already Have.

medium.com

TOOLS

Create Video Receipts for AI Agents with Playwright Screencast API

Anton Gulin describes Playwright v1.59.0's new Screencast API, which records the session as a video with chapter markers and action labels that you can attach to a ticket.

medium.com

I Pointed Karpathy’s Autoresearch at My Test Coverage. Here’s What Happened.

Can you make AI work in a loop to automatically close the coverage gap? Chandni Kaithavalappil tried Karpathy's autoresearch on a small app and shares what happened.

Moreover, Irfan Mujagić explains how to go From CI Failure to Root Cause in Seconds: MCP for QA Engineers.

medium.com

Playwright Fixtures: Making Your Tests Clean, Smart & Scalable

If you don't want to write login steps in every Playwright test, Aparna Mishra breaks down how fixtures pair with POM to handle the test setup for you.

Also, Can Claude Skills Replace Playwright Agents? A Practical View for QA Engineers by Kailash Pathak.

medium.com

Type-safe SQL in Playwright tests: a compile-time FSM, a branded string, and zero leaked connections

Vitali Haradkou built three helpful solutions that bring SQL validation to Playwright tests, including compile-time checks on SQL queries, parameter inference from placeholders and automatic connection teardown.

Additionally, Reyad Hassan explains How to Mock APIs and Own Your Test Scenarios with Playwright.

blog-vitaliharadkous-projects.vercel.app

Your Cypress Tests Are Slower Than You Think

David Ingraham outlines why Cypress suites get gradually slower and shows a few tweaks that bring fast feedback back to your team.

Similarly, Vitaliy Potapov describes in detail how the Fully Parallel Mode in Playwright works.

medium.com

VIDEOS

9+ Software Testing Agents to Know

If you're curious about what agentic AI testing solutions are on the market right now, Daniel Knott gives a 15-minute high-level overview.

youtube.com

Playwright 1.59: AI Agent Debugger + Trace Analysis (New Features)

Playwright 1.59.0 is out with some exciting features that Artem Bondar discusses in this 19-minute recording.

Similarly, Alex Khvastovich also did his own overview of the Playwright 1.59 New Features You Should Know.

youtube.com

这是最受尊敬的咨询公司之一对工具、技术、平台、语言和框架的建议的半年快照。

它不仅对于发现趋势非常有用，而且对于识别潜在的风险和危险也非常有用。

如果您想知道这意味着什么，Patrick Prill 写了一篇精彩的总结 - 科技雷达正在闪烁红光。

测试愉快！

大卫·迪洛维奇

赞助商链接

Selenium 创建者谈 AI 测试、BiDi 和真实情况

如果您编写了 Selenium 测试，那么您就使用了 Jason Huggins 构建的东西。在 Breakpoint 2026 上，他谈论了测试的发展方向：BiDi、左移重新思考，以及 AI 演示与冲刺实际情况之间的差距。 5 月 12 日至 14 日免费在线加入。 保留您的位置！

browserstack.com

新闻

对软件质量、疑虑和您实际建立的职业生涯的 6 年反思

质量工程师的工作实际上如何随着经验而改变？ Shubham Sharma 回顾并反思对质量的看法、冒名顶替综合症以及为什么高级工程师能够更好地容忍不确定性。

此外，Swati Seela 分享了她对如何成为优秀 QA 主管的观点。

medium.com

现代测试的实用心理模型

不幸的是，我无法识别作者，他分享了一篇非常好的、深入的文章，提供了关于如何正确思考每一层测试的实用建议。

同样，Keith Klain 也提出了一些关于思考、快速、不的好观点。

medium.com

认知自动化：这与生成脚本的速度无关

您的 AI 生成的测试是否真的能捕获错误？ Simon Prior 提示质量问题人们希望使用人工智能作为风险和策略的思考伙伴，而不是更快地编写不稳定的测试。

西蒙还写了一篇关于质量文化：共享所有权现在更难，更不容易的好文章。

leadtestinclude.com

我已经找到了自己在人工智能时代的定位

Vernon Richards 撰写的一篇精彩而深思熟虑的文章，讲述了测试人员角色如何从实践工作演变为指导团队和指导 AI 代理。

同时，Gary Hawkes 解释了为什么质量工程师在人工智能时代很重要。

substack.com

瀑布反击

Patrick Prill 观察到一个有趣的模式 - 规范驱动开发要求开发人员预先编写完美的规范，这与我们承认在敏捷到来之前的瀑布时代我们不擅长的事情是一样的。

那么它会通向哪里呢？ Simon 随后发表了另一篇文章：我们正在构建正确的东西吗？或者 GenAI 如何让我们忘记询问。

wordpress.com

自动化

人工智能和测试：评估对话

如果您正在测试人工智能驱动的解决方案，Jeff Nyman 有一份实用指南，介绍如何使用 DeepEvals 检查模型是否在完整的多轮对话中保持其线程。

testerstories.com

API 是可预测的。人工智能不是。这是我构建的

想要阻止 AI 编写仅检查 200 响应的浅层 API 测试吗？ Wendy Erdheim-Poch 分享了一个分步工作流程，用于扫描路线、提出正确的问题并检查自己的输出。

此外，Josphine Job 就为什么每个 QA 都应该构建自己的 AI 工作空间分享了很好的建议。

medium.com

如何处理由已知错误导致的失败测试

虽然注释掉损坏的测试很容易，但这绝不是一个好主意。 David Mello 演示了如何使用跳过模式，而不是使用错误单链接和 Jest、Playwright、pytest 的现成片段d JUnit。

此外，Swati Seela 写了一篇关于测试自动化中的重试：安全网还是静默问题？

的深思熟虑的文章

davidmello.com

我的 2 美分：我很乐意花它们来停止盯着测试日志

厌倦了试图找出失败的测试是不稳定的还是显示出实际问题？ Giuseppe Donati 分享了 trivago 如何构建一个为他们服务的人工智能助手。

trivago.com

优化测试过程中的错误部分

Chris Kenst 继承了经过 2,500 次测试的 Cypress 套件，该套件需要 45 小时才能运行，并解释了为什么自动化一切会带来痛苦。

同样，Jitesh Gosai 很好地解释了数量决定质量。

kenst.com

将 UI 视为契约：消除现代开发中的等待

想要从第一天开始测试而不是等到结束吗？ 大卫·英格拉汉姆和莱昂纳多·兰尼 写了一篇深思熟虑的文章，解释了带有模拟数据的 UI 骨架如何让前端、后端和 QA 同时移动。

关于这一点，Marko Churlinoski 解释了为什么我们应该停止编写新测试。增强您已有的能力。

medium.com

工具

使用 Playwright Screencast API 为 AI 代理创建视频收据

Anton Gulin 介绍了 Playwright v1.59.0 的新 Screencast API，它将会话记录为带有章节标记和操作标签的视频，您可以将其附加到票证上。

medium.com

我将 Karpathy 的自动研究指向了我的测试覆盖率。这就是发生的事情。

你能让人工智能循环工作以自动缩小覆盖范围差距吗？ Chandni Kaithavalappil 在一个小应用上尝试了 Karpathy 的autoresearch 并分享了所发生的情况。

此外，Irfan Mujagić 解释了如何在几秒钟内从 CI 失败到根本原因：QA 工程师的 MCP。

medium.com

剧作家装置：让您的测试干净、智能且可扩展

如果您不想在每个 Playwright 测试中编写登录步骤，Aparna Mishra 详细介绍了夹具如何与 POM 配对来为您处理测试设置。

此外，克劳德技能可以取代剧作家经纪人吗？ QA 工程师的实用观点，作者：Kailash Pathak。

medium.com

Playwright 测试中的类型安全 SQL：编译时 FSM、品牌字符串和零泄漏连接

Vitali Haradkou 构建了三个有用的解决方案，将 SQL 验证引入 Playwright 测试，包括 SQL 查询的编译时检查、占位符的参数推断和自动连接拆卸。

此外，Reyad Hassan 解释了如何使用 Playwright 模拟 API 并拥有您的测试场景。

blog-vitaliharadkous-projects.vercel.app

您的 Cypress 测试比您想象的要慢

David Ingraham 概述了为什么Cypress 套件逐渐变慢，并展示了一些调整，可以为您的团队带来快速反馈。

同样，Vitaliy Potapov 详细描述了Playwright 中的完全并行模式的工作原理。

medium.com

视频

9+ 软件测试代理知识

如果您对目前市场上有哪些代理 AI 测试解决方案感到好奇，Daniel Knott 会提供 15 分钟的高级概述。

youtube.com

Playwright 1.59：AI 代理调试器 + 跟踪分析（新功能）

Playwright 1.59.0 推出了一些令人兴奋的功能，Artem Bondar 在这个 19 分钟的录音中讨论了这些功能。

同样，Alex Khvastovich 还对您应该了解的 Playwright 1.59 新功能做了自己的概述。

youtube.com

并且...

如果您正在进行测试自动化，那么您并不是真正在测试... 💡

感谢您的阅读！

item.title: 【Software Testing Weekly - Issue 309 - Apr 20th 2026】软件测试周刊 - 第 309 期 - 2026 年 4 月 20 日
item.description:
【

COMMENT

Welcome to the 309th issue!

Looking for a software testing tool?

Check out TestVerse — a free directory of categorised 190+ testing tools by Anshita Bhasin.

And if you want to learn more about how to use it, she wrote a handy guide.

Happy testing! 🙂

Dawid Dylowicz

Sponsored Link

Coding agents Are Shipping 55% Faster. Keep Up at the Agentic Testing Summit.

The outer loop has become the new bottleneck for AI-generated code. Join mabl and QA leaders for a half-day summit to learn how to build an agentic testing strategy, network with peers who are experimenting with new approaches, and leave with a clearer picture of how your team stays ahead. Register for a summit near you.

mabl.com

NEWS

AI Is Changing Software Testing. After 20 Years in QA, I Can Tell You This Shift Is Different.

Olga Manuilova reflects on 20 years in QA and explains how the profession is moving from execution toward quality strategy and risk management.

Additionally, Simon Prior shares some fresh thoughts on Intelligent Quality Leadership: A Model Still Taking Shape.

medium.com

Quality Isn't a Testing Problem

A good reminder from Alan Page that quality lives in the system and it should be built-in, rather than tested-in.

This is followed by a fantastic post from Filip Hric about Maslow's Hammer and Three Lies QA Tells Itself.

substack.com

Rethinking Your Test Strategy for AI-Powered Features

Testing AI features? Irfan Mujagić shares a test strategy, including a practical framework for deciding what to automate, what to check manually and what to monitor.

You can also follow Emily O'Connor and Richard Adams's advice on Two ways to use the "5 whys" method: Root cause of bugs and identifying continuous improvements.

thegreenreport.blog

Testing Is Systems Thinking

A thought-provoking article by Patrick Prill describing how to use the DSRP mental model (Distinctions, Systems, Relationships, Perspectives) for better testing.

Moreover, Patrick also explains why AI Cannot Replace Glue Work.

wordpress.com

You Climbed the Test Pyramid. Now Eat a Custard Slice.

What if you thought about your test suite by the value each layer provides, not just the technical scope? Stuart Crocker introduces the Custard Slice as an alternative to the Test Pyramid.

At the same time, Shubham Sharma came up with The Testing Lattice — a handy way of assessing your testing maturity.

dragonsforelevenses.com

AUTOMATION

How AI Testing Agents Are Transforming QA at Showpad

Looking for advice on how to embed AI agents into daily QA work? Ganeshan Manickam describes how they built small agents for each testing phase and what they learned from that.

medium.com

The Chaos Mutant: What if a Bot Tried to Break Your Code Every Night?

Prateek Singh gives an overview of a nightly mutation testing setup that randomly picks recently changed files, injects bugs and shows which ones your tests would miss.

Also, Thulane Khumalo asks and explains: What are semtests?

medium.com

The 'valuable' in valuable feedback, fast

What makes a good test automation? Bas Dijkstra breaks it down into four angles and shares practical tips, such as keeping the test scope small and using custom assertion messages. Bas also shared My thoughts on 'self-healing' in test automation.

ontestautomation.com

Why Layered Test Framework Architecture Still Matters in the Age of AI

Josphine Job goes through the six layers of a test automation framework and explains why AI doesn't replace them but adds an orchestration layer on top.

Moreover, Mohammad Faisal Khatri shows an example of implementing Builder Pattern + Faker in API Test Automation using Playwright with TypeScript.

medium.com

You Write Too Many Tests

If you don't have confidence in your integration tests, Chris Tonkinson explains why you should probably have fewer of them and use a Scenario Tree Testing pattern for top-down coverage instead.

Similarly, Oliver Fries describes how I stopped treating testing methodologies as religion and started treating them as tools in the context of TDD and BDD.

medium.com

TOOLS

Creating a resilient test framework with the Playwright Page Object Model (POM)

If you want to build a test framework that scales, Shawn Vernier shows a Page Object Model setup with examples in Playwright.

A great additional read to that is Aparna Mishra's take on Playwright POM (Without Classes): Make Your Tests Clean & Reusable.

ministryoftesting.com

Playprom: Turn your Playwright test run into a time-series data

Want to see your Playwright test results over time? Lutfi Fitroh Hadi built Playprom — a reporter that emits test runs as metrics into Prometheus and Grafana.

Similarly, Vitali Haradkou created a handy solution for Playwright test reports that actually look good in email.

medium.com

Playwright Accessibility Testing: What axe and Lighthouse Miss

If you're using automated tools for accessibility testing, you may be interested to learn from David Mello which defects scanners can't catch and how to leverage Playwright for better results.

And if you use Cypress, Gleb Bahmutov has also got you covered: Testing A11y Using Cypress And wick-a11y Plugin.

davidmello.com

Playwright MCP Vision + DevTools: AI Agents That See the Page AND Read Network Traffic Simultaneously

Do you know about Playwright MCP's capability modes? Pramod Dutta gives an overview of snapshot, vision, and devtools with practical examples of when to use each one and how to combine them.

Moreover, Gurudatt S A tells us Why Your Playwright getByRole Locator Isn't Working — Understanding ARIA and Accessible Names.

medium.com

UTML: A UI Test Markup Language for Browser Automation

Kulanthaivelu Sankaran proposes UTML, a JSON-based markup language for browser tests, which you can use to describe steps, such as "click Sign in button", and let it handle the rest. You can also read part 2 and part 3.

medium.com

BOOKS

Reading of The Staff Engineer's Path

This is a thoughtful reflection from Roy Straub after rereading The Staff Engineer's Path now that he's become a Tech Lead and has a different perspective.

rstraub.com

VIDEOS

From Developer to Tester: Navigating the Shift in an AI-Driven Testing World

An insightful, 46-minute discussion between David Burns and Benjamin Bischoff about the evolving role of software testers in the AI-powered world.

Similarly, Alan Richardson invited Krisztián Fischer and Toby Sears to talk about AI and Software Testing.

youtube.com

How to identify risks which matter most for testing

Vitaly Sharovatov started a new series of recordings, supported by blog posts, about risks in software testing. This 11-minute recording is followed by another one about How to prioritize risks for testing.

qase.io

AND...

Codex will review your code... 😂

Thanks for reading!

If you enjoy this newsletter and find it helpful in becoming a better tester, please consider sharing it with others.

Dawid Dylowicz

This RSS feed is published on https://softwaretestingweekly.com/. You can also subscribe via email.

】

评论

欢迎来到第309期！

正在寻找软件测试工具？

查看 TestVerse — 由 Anshita Bhasin 提供的包含 190 多种分类测试工具的免费目录。

如果您想了解有关如何使用它的更多信息，她编写了一份方便的指南。

测试愉快！ 🙂

大卫·迪洛维奇

赞助商链接

编码代理的发货速度加快了 55%。继续参加代理测试峰会。

外循环已成为人工智能生成代码的新瓶颈。与 mabl 和 QA 领导者一起参加为期半天的峰会，了解如何构建代理测试策略，与正在尝试新方法的同行建立联系，并在离开时更清楚地了解您的团队如何保持领先地位。 报名参加您附近的峰会。

mabl.com

新闻

人工智能正在改变软件测试。经过 20 年的 QA 工作，我可以告诉您这种转变是不同的。

Olga Manuilova 回顾了 20 年的 QA 经验，并解释了该行业如何从执行转向质量战略和风险管理。

此外，Simon Prior 分享了关于智能质量领导力：仍在形成的模型的一些新想法。

medium.com

质量不是测试问题

Alan Page 的一个很好的提醒，系统的质量生活，它应该是内置的，而不是经过测试的。

接下来是 Filip Hric 发表的一篇关于马斯洛之锤和 QA 的三个谎言的精彩帖子。

substack.com

重新思考 AI 支持的功能的测试策略

测试人工智能功能？ 伊尔凡·穆贾吉奇 分享一个测试策略，包括一个实用的框架，用于决定什么要自动化、什么要手动检查以及什么要监视。

您还可以按照Emily O'Connor和Richard Adams关于使用“5个为什么”的两种方法的建议方法：错误的根本原因并确定持续改进。

thegreenreport.blog

测试是系统思考

Patrick Prill 发表的一篇发人深省的文章，描述了如何使用 DSRP 心理模型（区别、系统、关系、视角）进行更好的测试。

此外，Patrick 还解释了为什么人工智能无法取代胶水工作。

wordpress.com

您爬上了测试金字塔。现在吃一块蛋奶冻片。

如果您根据每层提供的价值来考虑测试套件，而不仅仅是技术范围，结果会怎样？ Stuart Crocker 介绍了蛋奶冻切片作为测试金字塔的替代方案。

同时，Shubham Sharma 提出了测试格 - 一种评估测试成熟度的便捷方法。

dragonsforelevenses.com

自动化

AI 测试代理如何改变 Showpad 的质量保证

正在寻求有关如何将 AI 代理嵌入到日常 QA 工作中的建议？ Ganeshan Manickam 描述了他们如何为每个测试阶段构建小型代理以及他们从中学到了什么。

medium.com

混沌突变体：如果机器人每天晚上都试图破解您的代码怎么办？

Prateek Singh 概述了夜间突变测试设置，该设置随机挑选最近更改的文件、注入错误并显示您的测试会错过哪些文件。

此外，Thulane Khumalo 询问并解释：什么是 semtest？

medium.com

快速提供有价值的反馈

什么才是好的自动化测试？ Bas Dijkstra 将其分为四个角度并分享实用技巧，例如保持较小的测试范围和使用自定义断言消息。 Bas 还分享了我对测试自动化中“自我修复”的想法。

ontestautomation.com

为什么要分层测试框架人工智能时代架构仍然很重要

Josphine Job 详细介绍了测试自动化框架的六层，并解释了为什么人工智能没有取代它们，而是在顶部添加了一个编排层。

此外，Mohammad Faisal Khatri 展示了使用 Playwright 和 TypeScript 在 API 测试自动化中实现Builder Pattern + Faker 的示例。

medium.com

您编写了太多测试

如果您对集成测试没有信心，Chris Tonkinson 解释了为什么您应该减少集成测试，并使用场景树测试模式进行自上而下的覆盖。

类似地，Oliver Fries 描述了我如何停止将测试方法视为宗教，并开始将它们视为 TDD 和 BDD 背景下的工具。

medium.com

工具

使用 Playwright 页面对象模型 (POM) 创建弹性测试框架

如果您想构建一个可扩展的测试框架，Shawn Vernier 会在 Playwright 中展示页面对象模型设置和示例。

对此的一个很好的补充阅读是Aparna Mishra对Playwright POM（没有类）：使您的测试干净且可重用的看法。

ministryoftesting.com

Playprom：将 Playwright 测试运行转换为时间序列数据

想要查看一段时间内您的剧作家测试结果吗？ Lutfi Fitroh Hadi 构建了 Playprom - 一个将测试运行作为指标发送到 Prometheus 和 Grafana 的报告器。

同样，Vitali Haradkou为剧作家测试报告创建了一个方便的解决方案，在电子邮件中看起来确实不错。

medium.com

剧作家无障碍测试：斧头和灯塔错过了什么

如果您使用自动化工具进行辅助功能测试，您可能有兴趣向 David Mello 学习哪些扫描仪无法捕获的缺陷以及如何利用剧作家以获得更好的结果。

如果您使用 Cypress，Gleb Bahmutov 也可以帮助您：使用 Cypress 和 wick-a11y 测试 A11y插件。

davidmello.com

剧作家 MCP Vision + DevTools：同时查看页面和读取网络流量的 AI 代理

你知道剧作家MCP的能力模式吗？ Pramod Dutta 概述了快照、愿景和开发工具，并提供了何时使用每种工具以及如何组合它们的实际示例。

此外，Gurudatt SA 告诉我们为什么你的剧作家 getByRole 定位器不起作用 - 了解 ARIA 和可访问名称。

medium.com

UTML：用于浏览器自动化的 UI 测试标记语言

Kulanthaivelu Sankaran 提出了 UTML，这是一种用于浏览器测试的基于 JSON 的标记语言，您可以使用它来描述步骤，例如“单击登录按钮”，并让它处理其余的事情。您还可以阅读第 2 部分和第 3 部分。

medium.com

书籍

资深工程师之路解读

这是 Roy Straub 在重读主管工程师之路后的深思熟虑的反思，现在他已经成为技术主管并拥有不同的观点。

rstraub.com

视频

从开发人员到测试人员：引领人工智能驱动的测试世界的转变

David Burns 和 Benjamin Bischoff 就软件测试人员在人工智能驱动的世界中不断变化的角色进行了长达 46 分钟的富有洞察力的讨论。

同样，Alan Richardson 邀请 Krisztián Fischer 和 Toby Sears 谈论人工智能和软件测试。

youtube.com

如何识别对测试最重要的风险

Vitaly Sharovatov 开始了一系列关于软件测试风险的新录音，并得到博客文章的支持。这段 11 分钟的录音之后是另一段关于如何确定测试风险优先级的录音。

qase.io

并且...

Codex 将审核您的代码... 😂

感谢您的阅读！

如果您喜欢本新闻稿并发现它有助于成为更好的测试人员，请考虑与其他人分享。

大卫·迪洛维奇

item.description:
【

COMMENT

Welcome to the 308th issue!

How should we approach testing in the age of AI?

It's an increasingly important question we should be asking ourselves.

So today, I want to highlight this great, thought-provoking article by Carlos Arguelles, Senior Principal Engineer at Amazon:

The Outer Loop is Dead: Rethinking how we test.

Happy testing!

Dawid Dylowicz

Sponsored Link

Breakpoint 2026: Where QA Teams Figure Out AI Together

Most teams are navigating AI-driven testing without a playbook. Breakpoint 2026 is where QA leaders from NVIDIA, Mastercard, KPMG, Deloitte, and Microsoft share what's actually working — live sessions, real Q&A, and hands-on workshops. Join from wherever you are on 12–14 May 2026. Save your spot!

browserstack.com

NEWS

Drop the test column. Now what?

Ah, the famous "In Testing" column! There are pros and cons to it, and if you're thinking about removing it, Jitesh Gosai suggests which signals to put in place to keep work visible.

In relation to that, Shawn Vernier wrote a good article on Why software testers should write documentation even if no one else reads it.

substack.com

Should QA exist?

Controversial! Jade Rubick wrote on whether engineering orgs should have QA at all, sparking an intriguing discussion among the testing community.

On that note, someone also asked: With AI advancing so fast… is Developer or QA the safer career now?

rubick.com

Testing the "Yes-Man" in Your Pocket

This is a sobering read from Jeff Nyman on why AI is biased towards agreeing with you and why the evaluation should be broader than just user satisfaction scores.

That's why Huib Schoots says we should value Critical Thinking and Bram van den Reijen explains why Being right is not enough: testing, truth and responsibility.

testerstories.com

The Code Tsunami

Vernon Richards reflects on how being a tester is becoming less about providing information and more about designing the decision framework that enables others to release safely.

Similarly, Andrii Cheparskyi talks about The Hidden Cost of AI-Generated Test Code, while Gil Zilberfeld explains why The Knowledge Void Eats Quality for Breakfast.

substack.com

You're Not Meta: Build Fast Teams with Fast Tests

An interesting read from Sayo Oladeji who advises investing in faster local test execution, fewer flaky tests and a balanced test pyramid, based on lessons learned at Google and Meta.

Moreover, Sanjeev Kumar tells us How I measure quality without looking at bug counts.

medium.com

AUTOMATION

AI in Test Automation: Real Limitations vs. User Error

David Mello reviews the most common AI testing complaints and confirms or debugs them, noting whether they're caused by AI or people.

Moreover, Pramod Dutta explains Why AI Made QA Engineers Write MORE Code, Not Less.

davidmello.com

AI-Powered API Testing at Scale

Wondering how to develop and run API tests across several repositories? Nikhil Gupta shows how to achieve that with an AI-powered approach.

Similarly, Olamide Adebayo describes how We Replaced Hours of Manual API Testing With an AI Agent Running Integration Tests in Real Time.

medium.com

The Bottom-Up Secret to 100% Test Coverage at Enterprise Scale

Is 100% coverage even possible? Alexandre Mendes also doubted it because it feels impossible when you think top-down, but becomes easier when you compose upward from smaller pieces.

On top of that, Doğukan Aydoğdu shares insights into How We Build Bulletproof Integration Tests.

medium.com

Writing More Readable Tests

Solid post from Ürgo Ringo on emphasising what matters and what doesn't in test code. Especially handy now that LLMs benefit from readable tests too.

Speaking of that, someone asked the testing community: Performing Assertions within the Page Object itself — is it a good idea?

medium.com

TOOLS

Designing Realistic Load Test Scenarios with k6

Indra Aristya shows how to design k6 load tests that mimic actual user behaviour with gradual ramp-up, sustained peak, ramp-down and think time between actions. Much more meaningful than a flat 100 VUs.

What's more, Bob Chen describes in three parts why K6.js API Health Tests Are Not a Testing Problem.

medium.com

I Built a QA Quality Gate System With Claude Code Hooks. Every AI-Generated Test Now Passes My Standards Before It Exists.

Wondering how to stop Claude from writing tests with hardcoded credentials and CSS selectors? Pramod Dutta demonstrates how he set up four hooks as predictable quality gates.

medium.com

Playwright Fixture Scopes: Know When to Use What

I wonder if you're aware of this handy feature in Playwright fixtures. Gurudatt S A covers how and when to use the test, worker, and file scopes.

Moreover, Viatsheslav Pashanin advises on Eliminating Authentication Overhead in Playwright Automation.

medium.com

Testing LLM Outputs: A Hands-On Guide to DeepEval Metrics

Serhii Smetanskyi shares what each DeepEval metric actually does, what surprised him, and what he wishes someone had told him before starting. Great reference if you're testing LLM features.

Similarly, Katja Obring points out that The Hard Part of AI Evals Isn't the Tooling.

linkedin.com

WICK-DOM-OBSERVER: The Deterministic Cypress Plugin for Fast Spinners, Blinking Toasts, Optional Overlays

Tired of flaky Cypress tests caused by quickly changing web elements? Sebastian Clavijo Suero built a plugin that uses MutationObserver to catch those tricky UI elements in a deterministic way.

At the same time, Vitaly Skadorva describes how to do Accessible web testing with Cypress and Axe Core.

dev.to

BOOKS

Essential reading for people who are still responsible and serious in IT

Maaike Brinkhof shares five books that helped her think more critically about IT, AI hype, and productivity culture. From cognitive biases to the history of the Luddites, this is an interesting and somewhat unconventional reading list.

maaikebrinkhof.nl

Put quality at the centre of what you do — A Review of 'Out of the Crisis' by W. Edwards Deming

A short, useful review from Mike Harris of a classic quality management book Out of the Crisis that's still relevant decades later.

home.blog

VIDEOS

QA Job Market Reality Check

Once again, Alex Khvastovich is back with a regular overview of the QA job market, sharing insights and advice.

Additionally, Karthik KK shares a bit more about The AI Layoff Lie: What Big Tech Isn't Telling You.

youtube.com

AND...

Just an app update... 😂

Thanks for reading!

If you enjoy this newsletter and find it helpful in becoming a better tester, please consider sharing it with others.

Dawid Dylowicz

评论

欢迎来到第308期！

人工智能时代我们应该如何进行测试？

这是我们应该问自己的一个越来越重要的问题。

今天，我想重点介绍亚马逊高级首席工程师 Carlos Arguelles 撰写的这篇伟大的、发人深省的文章：

外循环已死：重新思考我们的测试方式。

测试愉快！

大卫·迪洛维奇

赞助商链接

2026 年断点：QA 团队共同探索人工智能

大多数团队在没有剧本的情况下进行人工智能驱动的测试。 Breakpoint 2026 是来自 NVIDIA、Mastercard、KPMG、Deloitte 和 Microsoft 的 QA 领导者分享实际工作成果的平台 - 现场会议、真实问答和实践研讨会。 2026 年 5 月 12 日至 14 日，无论您身在何处，都可以参加。保留您的席位！

browserstack.com

新闻

删除测试列。现在怎么办？

啊，著名的“测试中”专栏！它有利有弊，如果您正在考虑删除它，Jitesh Gosai 建议放置哪些信号以保持工作可见。

与此相关，Shawn Vernier 写了一篇很好的文章，内容是为什么软件测试人员应该编写文档，即使没有其他人阅读它。

substack.com

应该存在质量检查吗？

有争议！ Jade Rubick 撰写了有关工程组织是否应该进行 QA 的文章，在测试社区中引发了一场有趣的讨论。

就此而言，有人还问：随着人工智能发展如此之快……现在开发人员还是 QA 是更安全的职业吗？

rubick.com

测试你口袋里的“唯唯诺诺”

这是 Jeff Nyman 的一篇发人深省的文章，解释了为什么人工智能偏向于同意你的观点，以及为什么评估应该更广泛，而不仅仅是用户满意度得分。

这就是为什么Huib Schoots说我们应该重视批判性思维和Bram van den Reijen 解释了为什么仅仅正确是不够的：测试、真相和责任。

testerstories.com

代码海啸

Vernon Richards 反思了作为一名测试人员如何不再仅仅提供信息，而更多地关注设计决策框架，使其他人能够安全地发布。

同样，Andrii Cheparskyi 谈论了人工智能生成的测试代码的隐性成本，而 Gil Zilberfeld 解释了为什么知识空白吃早餐的质量。

substack.com

你不是元：通过快速测试构建快速团队

Sayo Oladeji 的有趣读物，他根据 Google 和 Meta 的经验教训，建议投资于更快的本地测试执行、更少的不稳定测试和平衡的测试金字塔。

此外，Sanjeev Kumar 告诉我们如何在不查看错误数量的情况下衡量质量。

medium.com

自动化

测试自动化中的人工智能：实际限制与用户错误

David Mello 回顾了最常见的 AI 测试投诉并确认或调试它们，并指出它们是由 AI 还是人造成的。

此外，Pramod Dutta 解释了为什么 AI 让 QA 工程师编写更多代码，而不是更少。

davidmello.com

大规模人工智能驱动的 API 测试

想知道如何跨多个存储库开发和运行 API 测试？ Nikhil Gupta 展示了如何通过人工智能驱动的方法实现这一目标。

类似地，Olamide Adebayo 描述了我们如何用实时运行集成测试的 AI 代理取代了数小时的手动 API 测试。

medium.com

企业规模 100% 测试覆盖率的自下而上秘诀

100% 的覆盖率是否可能？ Alexandre Mendes 也对此表示怀疑，因为感觉不可能n 你是自上而下思考的，但当你从小块向上组合时会变得更容易。

除此之外，Doğukan Aydoğdu 分享了对我们如何构建防弹集成测试的见解。

medium.com

编写更具可读性的测试

来自 Ürgo Ringo 的可靠帖子，强调了测试代码中重要的内容和不重要的内容。现在法学硕士也受益于可读的测试，这尤其方便。

说到这里，有人问测试社区：在页面对象本身内执行断言 - 这是一个好主意吗？

medium.com

工具

使用 k6 设计真实的负载测试场景

Indra Aristya 展示了如何设计 k6 负载测试，通过逐渐上升、持续峰值、下降和操作之间的思考时间来模拟实际用户行为。比固定的 100 个 VU 更有意义。

此外，Bob Chen分三个部分描述了为什么K6.js API 健康测试不是测试问题。

medium.com

我使用 Claude Code Hooks 构建了 QA 质量门系统。现在，每个人工智能生成的测试在出现之前就已经通过了我的标准。

想知道如何阻止 Claude 使用硬编码凭据和 CSS 选择器编写测试？ Pramod Dutta 演示了他如何设置四个钩子作为可预测的质量门。

medium.com

剧作家固定范围：知道何时使用什么

我想知道您是否知道Playwright装置中的这个方便的功能。 Gurudatt S A 介绍了如何以及何时使用测试、工作人员和文件范围。

此外，Viatsheslav Pashanin 建议消除剧作家自动化中的身份验证开销。

medium.com

测试 LLM 输出：DeepEval 指标实践指南

Serhii Smetanskyi 分享了每个 DeepEval 指标的实际用途，w这让他感到惊讶，他希望有人在开始之前告诉他这件事。如果您正在测试 LLM 功能，这是很好的参考。

同样，Katja Obring 指出，AI 评估的困难部分不是工具。

linkedin.com

WICK-DOM-OBSERVER：用于快速旋转、闪烁 Toast、可选叠加的确定性 Cypress 插件

厌倦了因快速变化的网络元素而导致的片状 Cypress 测试？ Sebastian Clavijo Suero 构建了一个插件，它使用 MutationObserver 以确定性的方式捕获那些棘手的 UI 元素。

同时，Vitaly Skadorva 介绍了如何使用 Cypress 和 Ax Core 进行可访问的 Web 测试。

dev.to

书籍

对于仍然对 IT 行业有责任感和认真态度的人来说，这是一本必备读物

Maaike Brinkhof 分享了五本书，帮助她更加批判性地思考 IT、AI 炒作和生产力文化。从认知偏见到勒德分子的历史，这是一个有趣且有些非传统的阅读清单。

maaikebrinkhof.nl

将质量置于工作的中心 — W. Edwards Deming 对《走出危机》的评论

Mike Harris 对一本经典质量管理书籍走出危机进行了简短而有用的评论，几十年后仍然具有现实意义。

home.blog

视频

QA 就业市场现实检查

Alex Khvastovich 再次回归，定期概述 QA 就业市场，分享见解和建议。

此外，Karthik KK 分享了更多关于人工智能裁员谎言：大型科技公司没有告诉你的事情。

youtube.com

并且...

只是一个应用程序更新... 😂

感谢您的阅读！

如果您喜欢本新闻稿并发现它有助于成为更好的测试人员，请考虑与其他人分享。

item.title: 【Software Testing Weekly - Issue 307 - Apr 1st 2026】软件测试周刊 - 第 307 期 - 2026 年 4 月 1 日
item.description:
【

COMMENT

Welcome to the 307th issue!

AI is the hottest topic right now. And for a reason!

So today, I'm bringing to you two big discussions among the testing community:

  • Do you use any tools or AI for testing?
  • AI use cases for QA

As a bonus, I also recommend Chris Kenst's take on My AI Tooling Stack: The March 2026 Edition.

Happy testing!

Dawid Dylowicz

NEWS

AI writes the code. But who tests it?

Good question. Axel Kirchner makes the case that AI-assisted development doesn't reduce the need for quality assurance but changes where that work needs to happen.

Similarly, Irfan Mujagić also asks: Who Tests the Tests? AI, QA, and the Verification Paradox.

medium.com

Architecting for Scale: Why "Writing Tests" Is No Longer the Point

Karthik Sivakumar argues that the biggest drag on engineering velocity isn't bad code — it's poorly designed test infrastructure.

What's more, Betty Lin shares about What AI Still Cannot See in Software Quality (Part 1): Requirement Conflicts, followed by parts two, three and four.

medium.com

From SDET to AI-augmented Quality Engineer: Where AI Actually Belongs

Not all parts of test automation benefit from AI in the same way. Viktar Karanevich points to a few areas and shares an SDET transformation roadmap.

aiqualityengineer.cc

QA engineers who will be the most successful over the next five years

Wondering how to keep up with the changing world of software? Ben Fellows sees the tester role changing too and suggests what skills will be the most important.

Additionally, Neil Duggan points out why Your QA Team in 2028 Doesn't Look Like Your QA Team Today.

linkedin.com

Quality Engineering with AI

This is good advice from Callum Akehurst-Ryan on how QA teams should adapt their approach when developers are leaning heavily on AI assistance.

And there's a reason why Dan Belcher announces we live in The Most Exciting Moment in Software History due to the recent advancement of LLM models.

cakehurstryan.com

What I Actually Look For When I Interview QA Engineers (And How You Can Prepare)

Preparing for your next QA role? Bartosz Kustra breaks down what actually matters to interviewers in the current market.

Similarly, Joshua Bihun also advises on Hiring QA Engineers: Start With What You Actually Need.

medium.com

AUTOMATION

Evolving POM: From Page Objects to Agent-Friendly Design

This is a good walkthrough from Martín Marchetto on how to structure test code so that both humans and AI agents can work with it.

medium.com

From a long list to a clear signal: baseline-driven accessibility reporting

Accessibility test reports can be noisy, but Benjamin Bischoff and the Trivago team found a better, more actionable way of dealing with it.

trivago.com

Manual QA + AI = Automation Tester

Pramod Dutta ran an interesting experiment, observing manual testers implement test suites much faster without a traditional learning path, thanks to AI.

Also, Megan Ozanne wrote a good article about Coaching with code: using AI to learn how to automate tests.

medium.com

Stop Writing API Tests Manually — Let Your OpenAPI Spec Do the Work

David Mello presents a tool that generates API test cases directly from an existing contract and proves to be surprisingly good at covering edge cases.

davidmello.com

What If AI Could Tell QA What Your Pull Request Might Break?

An interesting idea from Mehmet Serhat Özdursun, suggesting using AI to analyse git diffs and give testers a structured view of where a change is most likely to cause problems.

devgenius.io

Sponsored Link

If there's one workshop this year that will genuinely change how you approach AI testing, this is it.

Join Ivan Davidov and Debbie O'Brien on April 29 for a hands-on deep dive into building Playwright architectures where AI actually works reliably at scale. This is the session your testing workflow has been missing.

Limited seats, use code PLAYWRIGHT40 for 40% off.

👉 Register now before it sells out.

eventbrite.com

TOOLS

3 Design Principles for Creating Agent Skills

Skills have become the default way to provide context and instructions to AI agents. But how to do it right? Angie Jones shares some tips.

Similarly, Gurudatt S A advises to Stop Re-Explaining Your Test Conventions to Claude — Use SKILL.md and Deep Shah explains why I Stopped Writing Prompts Every Day.

angiejones.tech

GitHub Copilot in QA — What Nobody Tells You Until You're Already Using It

Swati Sabharwal spent six months figuring out how to make AI coding assistance work in a real team environment and shares her insights.

Speaking of that, James Kip explains why Your Linter Can't Save You: Using .github/copilot-instructions.md to Catch What Static Analysis Misses.

medium.com

Maestro at Scale: Architecting a Deterministic Mobile Test Platform

Emre Erkek describes in detail how they implemented an end-to-end mobile automation with Maestro across multiple business domains.

medium.com

Migrating from Selenium to Playwright: The Complete Guide

Thinking about switching to Playwright? Asjad Khan wrote an extensive overview on how to do it right, especially about the challenging parts.

currents.dev

VIDEOS

I Built Karpathy's AutoResearch for Playwright Testing

In this 10-minute overview, Karthik KK demonstrates a custom-built autonomous UI testing agent with Playwright, inspired by autoresearch's approach.

youtube.com

Playwright CLI Tutorial

Playwright CLI was released just a few weeks ago and it's now the default interface for AI agents. If you want to see it in action, Lucas Smit recorded a helpful 18-minute demo.

youtube.com

AND...

Bugs in 2026... 😅

Thanks for reading!

If you enjoy this newsletter and find it helpful in becoming a better tester, please consider sharing it with others.

Dawid Dylowicz

人工智能是当前最热门的话题。这是有原因的！

所以今天，我将为您带来测试社区中的两个重大讨论：

  • 您是否使用任何工具或人工智能进行测试？
  • 用于质量检查的人工智能用例

作为奖励，我还推荐 Chris Kenst 对我的 AI 工具堆栈：2026 年 3 月版的看法。

测试愉快！

大卫·迪洛维奇

新闻

AI 编写代码。但谁来测试它呢？

好问题。 Axel Kirchner 证明人工智能辅助开发并没有减少质量保证的需求，而是改变了需要进行工作的地方。

同样，Irfan Mujagić 也问：谁来测试测试？人工智能、质量保证和验证悖论。

medium.com

规模化架构：为什么“编写测试”不再是重点

Karthik Sivakumar 认为，工程速度的最大拖累并不是糟糕的代码，而是设计糟糕的测试基础设施。

此外，Betty Lin 分享了人工智能在软件质量中仍然看不到的东西（第 1 部分）：需求冲突，随后是两部分， 三个和四个。

medium.com

从 SDET 到 AI 增强质量工程师：AI 的真正归属

并非测试自动化的所有部分都以同样的方式受益于人工智能。 Viktar Karanevich 指出了几个领域并分享了 SDET 转型路线图。

aiqualityengineer.cc

未来五年内最成功的 QA 工程师

想知道如何跟上不断变化的软件世界？ Ben Fellows 发现测试人员的角色也在发生变化，并建议哪些技能是最重要的。

此外，Neil Duggan 指出了原因2028 年的 QA 团队与今天的 QA 团队不同。

linkedin.com

人工智能质量工程

这是 Callum Akehurst-Ryan 提出的关于当开发人员严重依赖人工智能辅助时 QA 团队应如何调整其方法的好建议。

Dan Belcher 宣布我们生活在软件历史上最激动人心的时刻，这是有原因的，因为 LLM 模型的最新进展。

cakehurstryan.com

面试 QA 工程师时我实际上在寻找什么（以及如何准备）

正在为您的下一个 QA 角色做准备吗？ Bartosz Kustra 详细分析了当前市场中对面试官来说真正重要的因素。

同样，Joshua Bihun 也就雇用 QA 工程师：从您实际需要的开始提出建议。

medium.com

自动化

不断发展的 POM：从页面对象到代理友好的设计

这是 Martín Marchetto 的一个很好的演练，介绍了如何构建测试代码，以便人类和 AI 代理都可以使用它。

medium.com

从长长的列表到清晰的信号：基线驱动的无障碍报告

辅助功能测试报告可能会很混乱，但 Benjamin Bischoff 和 Trivago 团队找到了一种更好、更可行的处理方法。

trivago.com

手动 QA + AI = 自动化测试仪

Pramod Dutta 进行了一项有趣的实验，观察手动测试人员在没有传统学习路径的情况下更快地实现测试套件，这要归功于人工智能。

此外，Megan Ozanne 写了一篇关于指导代码：使用 AI 学习如何自动化测试的好文章。

medium.com

停止手动编写 API 测试 - 让您的 OpenAPI 规范来完成工作

大卫·梅洛 提出了一种直接从现有合约生成 API 测试用例的工具，并且事实证明在覆盖边缘情况方面出人意料地出色。

davidmello.com

如果人工智能可以告诉 QA 你的 Pull 请求可能会破坏什么？

来自 Mehmet Serhat Özdursun 的一个有趣想法，建议使用 AI 来分析 git diff，并为测试人员提供结构化视图，了解更改最有可能导致问题的位置。

devgenius.io

赞助商链接

如果说今年有一个研讨会能够真正改变您进行 AI 测试的方式，那就是它了。

4 月 29 日与 Ivan Davidov 和 Debbie O'Brien 一起深入实践，深入构建 Playwright 架构，让 AI 能够在规模上真正可靠地运行。这是您的测试工作流程缺少的会话。

席位有限，使用代码PLAYWRIGHT40可享受 40% 的折扣。

👉在售完之前立即注册。

【

COMMENT

Welcome to the 304th issue!

Big news! Meta announces a new testing method — Just-in‑Time Tests (JiTTests).

It's a new way of unit testing at scale thanks to the LLM-powered mutation technique.

The idea is simple — let AI generate lots of unit tests to catch possible failures, and then delete them.

Here's a 17-page research paper describing in detail why and how it works.

Also, Ayyaz Zafar summarises it: Meta's JiTTests: How AI Writes 22,000 Tests, Finds 4x More Bugs, Then Deletes Them All.

Happy (just-in-time) testing! 🙂

Dawid Dylowicz

Sponsored Link

These three BrowserStack AI Agents are changing how website QA works

BrowserStack's Website Scanner now has agents that don't just flag problems, they investigate them. Catch hidden accessibility gaps, get code-level fix guidance straight from your DOM, and reduce visual review time by 3x. Three agents, one scan, and fewer questions when it's time to ship. Scan your website for free!

browserstack.com

NEWS

Achieving Continuous Quality: Building a Culture That Lives and Breathes Value

Want to create a culture of quality in your team? Stuart Day shares how to go beyond mere testing activities and build a strong quality mindset and practice.

Similarly, Joshua Bihun describes what it takes to move towards Quality Assistance: Reframing QA From Gatekeeper to Coach.

medium.com

Development Got 10x Faster. Testing Didn't.

Hürkan Tuna raises a valid concern — it's becoming increasingly easier to build software faster, but proper verification and tracking are harder to scale. You can read more about it in the second part and the third part.

And, as Arik Aharoni points out, this creates a need for a new role — Test Critic: Navigating the AI Coverage Tsunami.

medium.com

Epistemic Testing: Chapter 4 — Who Tests the Tester?

Testing isn't just code — it's a mirror of your assumptions. Masoud Bahrami explores how doubt, curiosity, and bias influence every test you write.

On that note, Matthew Sullivan outlines why Software is treacherous and how we can reclaim purpose and influence in testing.

masoudbahrami.com

What AI Does in My QA & Automation Workflow

Curious where AI actually supports daily QA work? Todd Conner breaks down how he uses it across planning, scripting and debugging, and where human judgment is still best.

At the same time, Stuart Thomas advises to Forget coverage; focus on risk.

medium.com

What is software quality?

That's a million-dollar question! And for a good reason, as the answer depends on context. Ady Stokes makes a great attempt at providing possible answers from various people and sources.

Similarly, Stuart Day emphasises Why the Language We Use About Quality Matters More Than We Think.

ministryoftesting.com

AUTOMATION

Automation Testing, The Hidden Cost of `data-testid` & the Business Impact

In this series of five articles, Vivek Munde brings up several points on how to correctly identify web UI elements for test automation. You can also read parts two, three, four and five.

medium.com

How we Engineered an AI Agent That Writes, Compiles, Executes, and Ships E2E Tests

If you're looking for a detailed description of how to build an agentic AI solution for auto-generating test automation, Shrey Vats has something for you. Find out more in the second, third and fourth parts.

Additionally, Vera Marczenko explains how to effectively Let AI Write Your Assertions — Then Validate Them With Your Own Patterns.

medium.com

Page Object Model Is Dead: Here's What Replaced It

A bold statement from Pramod Dutta, but there are some arguments supporting it, including how the Screenplay and App Action patterns can replace it.

On that note, I'd also like to highlight A Field Guide to Not Overengineering Test Automation by Irfan Mujagić.

medium.com

The Testing Pyramid: Everybody Knows It, Nobody Follows It

Serhii Smetanskyi lists common pitfalls when trying to follow the test pyramid and explains what to do at each layer to make it work.

Moreover, Okan Yurt explains why Coverage ≠ Quality: Rethinking Unit Tests in the Age of AI.

linkedin.com

Sponsored Link

AI in testing is solving the wrong problem

If AI isn't helping your testing, maybe your approach is already broken. Discover why new tools can undermine testing outcomes, and how optimizing for coverage instead of business risk can backfire fast. If you are using AI in testing, this is an essential read. Check it out

tricentis.com

TOOLS

Advanced Playwright Authentication: A Multi-Role Fixture for Scalable E2E Testing

Testing web app flows with authentication is often challenging. But there's a way to make it much easier, and Sajith Dilshan shows how to achieve that with Playwright.

Furthermore, Faizan Shaikh provides a few tips on proper Playwright Error Handling Explained: Common Errors, Strict Mode, and Best Practices.

medium.com

Clean API tests with Cypress aliases

Bart Vanherck demonstrates a helpful solution to make Cypress API tests much more concise and easier to write.

Similarly, Mohammad Faisal Khatri wrote a helpful guide on How to test POST API Requests with Playwright TypeScript.

thetestingpirate.be

Giving AI Eyes and Hands — Which Browser MCP Actually Works

Wondering which browser MCP fits your automation tasks? Andrii Cheparskyi ran a hands-on comparison across Playwright MCP, Chrome DevTools MCP and Agent Browser, measuring how they behave under test.

medium.com

How a Learning Project Became Our Modern Mobile Test Framework

Raymond Saba and Breno Bittencourt walk through their shift from a legacy setup to a modular Appium 2/3 solution with plugins, parallel threads and shared ownership.

What's more, Anthony Dawson demonstrates how Appium MCP Unlocks New Methodologies in Mobile Automation.

trivago.com

JavaScript Web Test Automation Framework Rankings in JavaScript Rising Stars 2025

Curious which test tools were the most trending on GitHub in 2025? Each year, there's a slight change, and there should be no surprise at the new contenders given the rise of AI-first tools. By Courtney Zhan.

substack.com

VIDEOS

Playwright MCP + LM Studio: Your Private AI Test Agent — No Rate Limits, No Cloud — JUST FREE!

In another great example, Karthik KK shows how to pair Playwright MCP with LM Studio to set up a local test agent without paying a dollar.

youtube.com

95% pass rate... 😂

Dawid Dylowicz

大新闻！ Meta 宣布了一种新的测试方法 - 即时测试 (JiTTests)。

得益于 LLM 支持的突变技术，这是一种大规模单元测试的新方法。

这个想法很简单——让 AI 生成大量单元测试来捕获可能的故障，然后删除它们。

这是一篇 17 页的研究论文，详细描述了它的工作原理和原理。

此外，Ayyaz Zafar 对其进行了总结：Meta 的 JiTTests：AI 如何编写 22,000 个测试，发现 4 倍以上的错误，然后将其全部删除。

快乐（及时）测试！ 🙂
